items.title: What Iran says is in the Donald Trump deal and the item 'removed from the agenda'
items.description: Iran agreeing to a ceasefire deal with the United States tells us Tehran likely had something to gain from signing on. This is what Iran is promoting as the 14-point deal.

items.title: Trump intensifies pressure on Netanyahu over Lebanon attacks
items.description: The US president levels more criticism at Israel's prime minister and suggests asking Syria to take on Hezbollah "if Israel can't do the job without killing everyone else".

items.title: Sandilands reaches settlement over $100m radio contract termination
items.description: Veteran Sydney broadcaster Kyle Sandilands and ARN Media reach a settlement to end a $100 million contract dispute, which had been playing out in the Federal Court.

items.title: Two men charged over alleged kidnapping murder of Sydney grandfather
items.description: Robbery and Serious Crime Squad detectives have charged another two men following an investigation into the alleged kidnapping and murder of Chris Baghsarian earlier this year in Sydney's north.

items.title: What a trillion dollars costs democracy
items.description: Democracy cannot survive trillionaires. We need to start taxing billionaires properly.

items.title: Live: Haaland double has Arnold's Iraq reeling, Mbappé scores screamer
items.description: Graham Arnold's Iraq takes on Erling Haaland and his highly-fancied Norwegian side in Boston after Kylian Mbappé's super strike sinks Senegal. Follow live.

items.title: Why the market thinks Michele Bullock is bluffing on rate hikes
items.description: Michele Bullock made it abundantly clear that the RBA was not ruling out further interest rate rises, but the market appears to be unswayed by the tough talk.

items.title: Live: ASX to slip, oil plunges to 3-month low on reports US to scale back Iran sanctions
items.description: Oil prices sink to a three-month low on reports the US will allow Iran to start selling oil again, while the Australian share market is likely to open lower after big falls across Wall Street's tech stocks. Follow live.

items.title: 'I didn't have a life': Pensioner moves to Thailand for cheaper living
items.description: Peter Stevenson says moving to Thailand has allowed him to live more comfortably on his Australian Age Pension after struggling to cover rent and essentials in regional Victoria.

items.title: Government to extend pay subsidy to avoid childcare worker walk-off
items.description: Early educators had threatened to walk off the job to keep a federally funded 15 per cent pay subsidy due to end in November.

items.title: Live: Australia lowers travel warning for Middle Eastern nations
items.description: Australia has lowered its travel advice warnings for several Middle Eastern countries following the signing of a ceasefire agreement between the US and Iran this week. Follow live.

items.title: Bluey speaks Yolŋu Matha for the first time
items.description: The animated award-winning cartoon series Bluey has been translated into Yolŋu Matha, from north-east Arnhem Land, for NAIDOC Week.

items.title: Gout runs a stunning third as Lyles breaks world record
items.description: Rising Australian superstar Gout Gout pushes American champion Noah Lyles all the way in their first race against each other.

items.title: Advocates call for a rethink on the factors driving male suicide
items.description: There are urgent calls for more customised support services for men and boys experiencing situational distress.

items.title: Lorne residents' invention a solution to town's marauding cockatoos
items.description: Residents of the scenic Great Ocean Road are at their wits' end after the increasingly intelligent birds learnt how to lift the lids of wheelie bins, spreading rubbish through the town of Lorne.

items.title: Six gaming experts share their favourite video games of the year so far
items.description: From cosy builders to hectic shooters and all the way through to nostalgic adventures, there are lots of gems to enjoy on your favourite game console so far this year.

items.title: What happened when Ann Patchett quit swearing for good
items.description: The bestselling author of books including Bel Canto, Tom Lake and her latest, Whistler, is determined to see the good in everyone.

items.title: Tim Wilson holds undisclosed shares in climate advisory firm through family trust
items.description: The shadow treasurer's investment trust holds 15,000 shares in a small company called Gondwana Carbon which helps developers to acquire land, develop carbon abatement projects, earn carbon credits and then trade them.

items.title: Prince George heading to Eton College to continue education
items.description: Prince George, who turns 13 in July, will attend Eton College this September, following in the footsteps of his father, Prince William.

items.title: After the first attempt failed, outback town gives renewables another go
items.description: This outback town is giving renewable energy another shot as a new solar farm and battery system hooks up to the grid, two decades after a solar array project failed to live up to the hype.

items.title: Police say man thankful after drug arrest halts lethal mushroom mix-up
items.description: A man dodges potentially fatal poisoning after allegedly mistaking lethal death cap mushrooms for their hallucinogenic counterparts while illegally foraging in southern Western Australia.

items.title: Dealing with NDIS leading to anxiety and suicidal ideation among participants
items.description: Participants say they are "exhausted" and "overwhelmed" by trying to navigate the complex and ever-changing NDIS system.

items.title: 'Unfair on him': Origin coaches back ref after gambling history revealed
items.description: Billy Slater and Laurie Daley come to the defence of referee Ashley Klein after his gambling debt history was revealed earlier in the week.

items.title: Qld government accused of campaign to remove Aboriginal people from health roles
items.description: The Queensland government will not deny the existence of "Project Invisibility", a name a barrister says is used internally to refer to the deliberate removal of Aboriginal people from leadership roles.

items.title: Women forced to labour in tearoom, run-down wards at NT's busiest hospital
items.description: From a mother forced to labour in a hospital's tearoom, to a baby sent home with jaundice on a busy night, doctors warn they are no longer able to provide NT patients with the standard of care they deserve.
